### Task Success Rate

The proportion of users who started a given task in CanadaLogin and reached that task's 
defined finishing point, measured from Google Analytics 4 funnel data.

This is a family of metrics, not a single number: each funnel declares its own task 
success rate as a `step_ratio` in its YAML definition on GitHub - one funnel step 
counted as the entry, another counted as the exit, both measured as GA4 `activeUsers` 
over the same reporting window. **The entry and exit steps for each funnel are 
described below as of this writing, but the YAML is the canonical, versioned source** - see
[`funnel_src/funnels/`](https://github.com/cds-snc/canadalogin-reporting-data-pipeline/tree/main/infra/modules/google_analytics/funnel_src/funnels) in the `canadalogin-reporting-data-pipeline` repo. 
Check the YAML before trusting a step name quoted here.

*Alternative names*:

- funnel completion rate
- task completion rate
- funnel success rate

#### Sign in

Funnel definition: [`sign_in.yaml`](https://github.com/cds-snc/canadalogin-reporting-data-pipeline/blob/main/infra/modules/google_analytics/funnel_src/funnels/sign_in.yaml).

Entry is the first taggable step of the sign-in flow (the "enter your email"
screen); exit is reaching MFA selection, the last step Google Analytics can
see. **This is not a full sign-in completion rate.** A successful sign-in
redirects off-site to IBM Verify and back to the relying party with no page in
between, so GA4 has no event to mark true completion - reaching MFA is the
closest proxy available. See the
[`funnels`](../catalog/google_analytics.qmd#funnels) catalog entry for the
`RESERVED_TOTAL` and `window_incomplete` conventions this table shares with
`funnel_metrics`.

#### Sign up

Funnel definition: [`sign_up.yaml`](https://github.com/cds-snc/canadalogin-reporting-data-pipeline/blob/main/infra/modules/google_analytics/funnel_src/funnels/sign_up.yaml).

Entry is the first step of the sign-up flow, after accepting Terms and
Conditions; exit is the account-creation confirmation screen. Unlike sign-in,
this **is** a true completion signal - the confirmation page is a real,
first-party GA4 event.

**Calculation.** Each funnel's task success rate is already computed and
stored as one row per window in
[`funnel_metrics`](../catalog/google_analytics.qmd#funnel_metrics): the
exit step's `activeUsers` divided by the entry step's, for that funnel run.
There is no ratio to compute by hand - filter to the funnel and metric, and
read `value`. Query
[`funnel_metrics_current`](../catalog/google_analytics.qmd#funnel_metrics_current)
rather than `funnel_metrics` directly, so a future funnel version bump can't
silently blend two definitions together. Filter `breakdown_value =
'RESERVED_TOTAL'` for the overall rate across all relying parties; substitute
a specific relying party name for a per-RP figure.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Example queries"}

::: {.panel-tabset}

## SQL

Sign in:

```sql
SELECT
    window_end,
    value AS task_success_rate
FROM google_analytics.funnel_metrics_current
WHERE funnel_id = 'sign_in'
  AND metric_id = 'task_success'
  AND window_days = '7'
  AND breakdown_value = 'RESERVED_TOTAL'
  AND NOT window_incomplete
  -- set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
  AND CAST(window_end AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2026-07-14' AND DATE '2026-08-03'
ORDER BY window_end;
```

Sign up:

```sql
SELECT
    window_end,
    value AS task_success_rate
FROM google_analytics.funnel_metrics_current
WHERE funnel_id = 'sign_up'
  AND metric_id = 'task_success'
  AND window_days = '7'
  AND breakdown_value = 'RESERVED_TOTAL'
  AND NOT window_incomplete
  -- set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
  AND CAST(window_end AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2026-07-14' AND DATE '2026-08-03'
ORDER BY window_end;
```

## R

Sign in:

```r
tbl(con, in_schema("google_analytics", "funnel_metrics_current")) |>
  filter(
    funnel_id == "sign_in",
    metric_id == "task_success",
    window_days == "7",
    breakdown_value == "RESERVED_TOTAL",
    !window_incomplete,
    # set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
    as.Date(window_end) >= as.Date("2026-07-14"),
    as.Date(window_end) <= as.Date("2026-08-03")
  ) |>
  select(window_end, task_success_rate = value) |>
  arrange(window_end)
```

Sign up:

```r
tbl(con, in_schema("google_analytics", "funnel_metrics_current")) |>
  filter(
    funnel_id == "sign_up",
    metric_id == "task_success",
    window_days == "7",
    breakdown_value == "RESERVED_TOTAL",
    !window_incomplete,
    # set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
    as.Date(window_end) >= as.Date("2026-07-14"),
    as.Date(window_end) <= as.Date("2026-08-03")
  ) |>
  select(window_end, task_success_rate = value) |>
  arrange(window_end)
```

:::

:::

*Interpretation notes.* The queries above use `window_days = '7'`, a rolling
weekly rate recomputed nightly on a 7-day window ending each date. Three window
lengths exist, and switching between them is a one-line change:

- `'1'` is the same metric on a single day. It is the noisiest of the three,
  but it is the only one that shows the exact date something changed.
- `'7'` is the usual default. Every window holds one of each weekday, so
  day-of-week effects wash out.
- `'28'` is a rolling four-week window. It is the steadiest of the three and
  the one to use for monthly reporting, but a step change takes 28 days to
  show up in it fully, so it is a poor way to check whether a fix worked.

All three are partition-key strings, not numbers, in this schema. Windows within
one `window_days` overlap, so consecutive rows are not independent readings: one
unusual day moves 7 weekly rows and 28 monthly ones. A `value` of `NULL` means
nobody reached the entry step that window (an undefined rate, not a true zero) -
such rows are rare but real, and an average that treats them as `0.0` will read
too pessimistic.

These two funnels are not directly comparable to each other: sign-in's rate
stops at MFA for the structural reason described above, so it reads lower than
a true completion rate would, while sign-up's rate is a real completion
figure. Comparing the two numbers as if they measured the same kind of finish
line will overstate the sign-in/sign-up gap.
